identity.title: Compositional Diffusion with Guided search for Long-Horizon Planning

problem.claim: Long-horizon planning with compositional generative models must combine local multimodal distributions without producing infeasible or globally incoherent plans.

gap.claim: Existing composition methods are described as averaging incompatible local modes when distributions are multimodal.

contributions.claim: The authors propose Compositional Diffusion with Guided Search (CDGS), embedding search within diffusion denoising to address mode averaging.
CDGS uses population-based sampling, likelihood-based pruning of infeasible candidates, and iterative resampling across overlapping segments to enforce global consistency.
The approach is applied across robot manipulation, panoramic image synthesis, and long video generation.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish CDGS by integrating guided search directly into the diffusion denoising process for compositional generation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that CDGS matches oracle performance on seven robot manipulation tasks and outperforms baselines lacking compositionality or long-horizon training data.
The authors report coherent text-guided panoramic images and long videos, attributing this to effective local-to-global message passing.

narrative_sequence.summary: Compositional generative models are presented as promising for modeling long-horizon task distributions with local modular models.
The abstract identifies mode averaging under multimodal local distributions as producing locally infeasible and globally incoherent plans.
CDGS embeds guided search in diffusion denoising and combines population sampling, likelihood filtering, and overlap-based resampling.
The authors report oracle-level performance on seven robot tasks and coherent generation in image and video domains.

source_observation.claim: The abstract aligns each proposed mechanism with a named failure mode: exploring local modes, pruning infeasible candidates, and resampling overlaps for global consistency.

lessons.interpretation: This provides a compact mechanism-to-failure mapping that makes the method's intended rationale inspectable.
lessons.application: When presenting a new planning method, pair each algorithmic component with the specific failure it is meant to mitigate, then report evidence at that level.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when component effects cannot be separately measured or when failures are not meaningfully decomposable.

unknowns: The abstract does not define the oracle, evaluation metrics, task details, baseline identities, or quantitative margins.
The reported cross-domain demonstrations omit dataset, comparison, and evaluation details, so their scope cannot be assessed from the abstract alone.
